name: Difference of two squares
note: Dominant operation: a difference. The shape is special — both chunks are perfect squares ($9 = 3^2$, $4x^2 = (2x)^2$). Recognising it unlocks factoring as $(a+b)(a-b)$.

name: Perfect square trinomial
note: Dominant operation: a sum of three terms. The shape is special: the middle term is twice the product of the roots of the outer terms. Recognising it unlocks writing as (a±b)².

name: Common factor
note: Dominant operation: a sum. The shape is special: all chunks share a factor (3, a, 2x, (x+1)). Recognising it unlocks factoring it out.

name: Linear form
note: Dominant operation: a sum. Highest power is 1 — one variable term and one constant. The linear shape.

name: Quadratic form
note: Dominant operation: a sum. Highest power is 2 — the quadratic shape. Recognising it gates all of quadratic algebra.
